# The provenance file on Krónos

*The provenance file for Krónos. Nothing here is unsourced; that is what the file is for.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **Κρόνος** — "Youngest Titan, personification of time, who castrated and deposed his father Uranus before being overthrown by his son Zeus". On record: LSJ, Beekes, Pape-Benseler, Hesiod, Theogony 166–210, 453–491, 617–735; Works and Days 109–126.

**2. The preserved evidence.** **o → ó** (Acute stress on the first omicron) — absent from the ASCII form *kronos*, present in the restoration, verifiable against the sources above.

**3. The narrative record.** **The Castration of Ouranos** — When Ouranos hid his and Gaia's children inside their mother, Gaia fashioned a great sickle of grey adamant and appealed to her sons.  Hesiod records the decisive detail: ‘all of them were glad in their hearts to hear the words of Gaia's treacherous speech — all, that is, but great-hearted Kronos, the crooked of counsel, who was the youngest’; the others feared their father, but Kronos the youngest dared (Theogony 166–172). **The Swallowed Children** — Power taught Kronos its oldest lesson: do to your children what was done to your father.  Warned by Gaia and starry Ouranós that he was fated ‘to be overthrown by his own son, strong though he was’, he kept constant watch, and Rhéā bore him Hestía, Deméter, Hēra, Hádēs, and Poseidôn — each of whom he swallowed whole, straight from the holy womb (Theogony 453–467; Apollodorus 1.

**4. The physical record.** At Olympia the Hill of Kronos (Kronion) rises above the sanctuary; Pausanias (6.20.1) records that the Eleans honor the god on its summit, and the Kronia was celebrated there in connection with the games' founding legend. Votive material from the precinct links the site to the old couple Kronos and Rhea. In Athens the Kronia marked the height of summer with its licensed inversion. At Rome, the Temple of Saturn in the Forum — vowed in the early Republic, rebuilt by L. Munatius Plancus in 42 BCE — housed the state treasury and the god's image bound in woolen fetters loosed for the Saturnalia; its surviving columns still stand at the foot of the Capitoline.

**5. The current holding.** The temple at [/kronos/](/kronos/), classified Tier 2. One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

**6. The documented resonances.** **Timekeeping & Calendar Systems**, **Agriculture, Food & Harvest**, **Ancestry & Heritage Services** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/kronos/blog/resonance/).

**7. The primary sources.** [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the library this file answers to, open at the [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/).

**8. The continuing record.** Krónos haunts Western imagination as Father Time.  Goya's Saturn Devouring His Son turned the myth into an image of mortality and madness.
